clue.text: Noteworthy waste was recyclable — feature of most 8s

definitions.note: 8 down is CLUE: most cryptic clues offer a definition and a piece of wordplay

indicators.note: something recyclable can be broken down and made into something new, so these three words are reworked into a fresh order

explanation.surface: An environmental remark that some notable rubbish could be recycled.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 1 across and 3 down. The cross-reference to 8 makes the definition a description of cryptic clues themselves, since most give the solver both a definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A typical cryptic clue gives its solver two routes in, a definition plus wordplay, as the puzzle's other themed entries spell out.

clue.text: False, outrageously dupe President first

indicators.note: first says the President's name comes before the rest

parts.note: Donald Trump, the US President

indicators.note: something done outrageously is wild and disordered, so the letters of dupe are rearranged

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the President is outrageously false and fools people first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False' sits at the front as the definition; 'first' puts the President ahead of the rearranged letters rather than signalling an initial letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A trumped-up charge is fabricated or invented, so the phrase is a synonym of false.

clue.text: Just emptied open lorry

indicators.note: a word emptied loses its contents, keeping just the outer letters of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A lorry that has just been emptied and left open.
explanation.definitionFit: Just and only are synonyms as adverbs, as in 'just two left'.

clue.text: See 1
Very broken-hearted at outset apparently having such a story?

parts.note: so means very, as in 'so sad'

indicators.note: at the outset means the start of broken-hearted is taken, its first letter only

explanation.surface: Someone heartbroken from the start seems to have a tale of woe to tell.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition works as a completion: a sob story is a tale told to win sympathy, and the whole clue suggests the teller of one.
explanation.definitionFit: A sob story is a tearful tale meant to draw pity, so the word fits as the kind of story.

clue.text: Request daily list for MPs

parts.note: to order is to request or demand
a daily is a newspaper published every day

explanation.surface: Asking for a newspaper's agenda for members of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: In the UK Parliament the order paper is the printed agenda of the day's business for MPs (Members of Parliament).
explanation.definitionFit: The order paper is the daily published agenda of parliamentary business, a schedule for members of the Commons.

clue.text: Shelter, perfect place when once lacking energy

indicators.note: lacking says the perfect place goes without the letter for energy

parts.note: heaven is the perfect place, paradise
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Shelter was once a perfect place, now drained of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a place of refuge or safety, a synonym of shelter.

clue.text: Cheek — that, going topless, authority figure needed?

parts.note: brass means cheek or nerve, as in 'the brass neck'

indicators.note: the word that loses its top, its first letter, when written in a down clue

explanation.surface: Someone's cheek is so great that an authority figure must step in.
explanation.walkthrough: A brass hat is informal British slang for a senior military officer, from the gold braid on the cap.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass hat is slang for a high-ranking officer, someone in charge, hence an authority figure.

clue.text: Signal to include large hint

indicators.note: to include says the signal holds the letter for large within it

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act, as for an actor
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A signal that carries a big hint.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue is a hint or pointer towards a solution.

clue.text: Money problems? Don't start!

indicators.note: telling problems not to start removes the word's first letter

parts.note: troubles are problems

explanation.surface: Someone sighs at the mention of money worries: don't get me started!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don't start!' reads as an exasperated plea but tells you to drop the first letter of the synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: Roubles are the currency of Russia, so the plural stands for money.

clue.text: Continually annoy, as it happens, old-fashioned society girl, on return

indicators.note: on return says the combined letters come back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: live means broadcast as it happens, in real time
a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman making her entrance into high society, a rather dated institution

explanation.surface: A dated socialite being a constant nuisance in real time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return' reverses LIVEDEB to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To bedevil is to plague or torment someone persistently, so it means to keep annoying.

clue.text: Initially serves up pleasant summer drinks

indicators.note: initially means the opening letter of each of the next four words is taken

explanation.surface: Someone serves up pleasant drinks for summer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to drink in small mouthfuls, so sups means sips or drinks as a verb.

clue.text: Being dry, replacement unfortunately left out

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of replacement are muddled, with one letter left out

explanation.surface: Bemoaning that a substitute was regrettably omitted.
explanation.walkthrough: Take L (left) out of REPLACEMENT, as 'out' says, and rearrange REPACEMENT, as 'unfortunately' says.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperance means abstinence from alcohol; to be dry is to be teetotal.

clue.text: No longer needed by group — a stand-in

indicators.note: needed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A band's substitute is no longer required.
explanation.definitionFit: Something past is over and gone, no longer current.

clue.text: Concierge unusually with load of time describing earth-based system?

indicators.note: unusually says the letters of concierge, with the extra one, are arranged in a non-standard way

explanation.surface: A hotel concierge oddly burdened with time, talking of some earthly system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with load of' just adds the T to the concierge's letters before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: A geocentric model places the Earth at the centre of the universe, an Earth-based scheme like Ptolemy's.

clue.text: Husband dined out like 13's 3

indicators.note: out says the letters of dined are put out of order

explanation.surface: A husband has gone out to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 down's answer (3 down) is concealed in its clue's words, so it is like that.
explanation.definitionFit: 13 down's solution lies concealed inside its clue's words, so it is a concealed answer.

clue.text: Superficial display taking everyone in

indicators.note: taking, with the later in, says the display takes everyone into itself
in completes taking in, putting everyone within the display

parts.note: a show is a display
all means everyone

explanation.surface: A superficial spectacle that fools everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... in' reads as deceiving, which suits a showy surface, but here it means holding something inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Shallow means lacking depth of thought, a synonym of superficial.

clue.text: Volume used by US associate in prosaic way

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of litre, a unit of volume
an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: An American and a partner using a book prosaically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' looks like a book but is the unit of capacity, spelt the US way.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally means in a plain, matter-of-fact sense, taking words at face value, without imagination.

clue.text: Promise fun as one route to 3

parts.note: giving your word is promising
play means fun or amusement

explanation.surface: Promising some fun as a way to reach a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 3 down is ANSWER: the wordplay is one of the two routes to it in a cryptic clue.
explanation.definitionFit: In a cryptic clue the letter-building part is one path a solver uses to reach the solution.

clue.text: Sulk pretty regularly

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter of pretty is taken, starting with the first

explanation.surface: Someone sulking quite often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pretty' looks like an adverb meaning rather, but it is the word letters are taken from.
explanation.definitionFit: A pet is a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet'.

clue.text: Scheme for small piece of land

definitions.meaning: a small area of ground, as for a vegetable garden

explanation.surface: A plan for a small allotment.
explanation.definitionFit: Plot means both a conspiratorial plan and a little patch of ground.

clue.text: Current very hot? Not right

indicators.note: not says the letter for right is taken away from the hot word

parts.note: tropical weather is very hot

explanation.surface: A query about whether a current is very hot, answered no.
explanation.definitionFit: Topical means relevant to present affairs, a synonym of current.

clue.text: Torment clergyman when initial resistance becomes hard

indicators.note: becomes says one letter is changed into another

parts.note: a rector is a clergyman in charge of a parish
R is the physics symbol for resistance, here the first letter
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Tormenting a vicar until his early resistance hardens.
explanation.definitionFit: To hector is to bully or harass someone with intimidating talk.

clue.text: Massaging ego — nut's way of speaking

indicators.note: massaging works something over, so the letters are kneaded into a new order

explanation.surface: Flattering a crank's ego is how a crazy person talks.
explanation.definitionFit: A tongue is a language, the way a people speaks.

clue.text: Meaning one route to 3

definitions.meaning: 3 down is ANSWER: the half of a cryptic clue giving a synonym is one way in

explanation.surface: Pondering the sense of one path to a solution.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a statement of sense, and also the half of a cryptic clue that equates directly to the solution.

clue.text: Costly address to partner

definitions.meaning: a term of endearment said to a spouse

explanation.surface: An expensive way of talking to your other half.
explanation.definitionFit: Dear means expensive, and is also a fond way of addressing a loved one.

clue.text: Small piece, not genuine, about learner

indicators.note: about says the fake goes round the learner

parts.note: fake means not genuine
L is the learner sign from British driving plates

explanation.surface: A tiny item, a counterfeit, concerning a pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A flake is a small thin fragment, as of snow or paint.

clue.text: Complain having lost English holdall

indicators.note: having lost says the complaint drops the letter for English

parts.note: to gripe is to complain

explanation.surface: Grumbling about a lost English bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A grip is an old-fashioned word for a travelling bag.

clue.text: Song from Callas maybe minutes away

indicators.note: away says the minutes letter is sent off

parts.note: Maria Callas was a famous opera soprano, so her first name is suggested

explanation.surface: A song by the great soprano lasting only minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera, the kind Callas famously sang.

clue.text: A horse run in morning like 30's 8

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
AM stands for ante meridiem, the morning

explanation.surface: A horse goes for a gallop in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 30 across's clue is a letter-rearrangement, so its 8 (CLUE) is this kind.
explanation.definitionFit: 30 across's clue is a rearrangement of letters, the device this word names.

clue.text: Island chap

definitions.meaning: the Isle of ... in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: A fellow from an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is the Isle of Man, a British Crown dependency, and also simply a male person.

clue.text: Brutal fellow, cur ultimately hostile in former colony

indicators.note: in says the cur's end and hostile go inside the former colony

parts.note: Goa was a Portuguese colony in India until 1961

indicators.note: ultimately means the final letter of cur is taken

parts.note: ill can mean unfriendly, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A brutish man and a hostile dog in an ex-colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorilla is used figuratively for a big, brutish thug.

clue.text: Newly re-enact entry as occasion for commemoration perhaps

indicators.note: newly means in a new way, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: Re-enacting a newly made entrance for a commemoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-hundredth anniversary is a typical event marked by a commemorative celebration.
